overall_summary: Metabolic marker reflecting glycemic status; shows significant decline post-COVID-19 infection in vaccinated survivors, with more pronounced improvement in males, indicating sex-specific metabolic recovery patterns.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significant reduction over time in both sexes, more pronounced in males (total cohort decreased from 126.00 to 113.60 mg/dL, p=0.017; males significantly declined, p=0.033).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Indicates improved glycemic control post-vaccination; supports need for early metabolic screening in males and sex-tailored monitoring strategies.

overall_summary: Long-term glycemic control marker; declines significantly post-COVID-19 in vaccinated survivors, with males showing higher baseline levels and more pronounced improvement.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significant reduction over time in both sexes, more pronounced in males (total cohort decreased from 7.26% to 6.43%, p<0.001). Males exhibited higher baseline levels.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Protective benefit in glycemic control, especially in males; supports prioritization of early metabolic screening in men post-COVID-19.

overall_summary: Thyroid-stimulating hormone; shows sex-specific endocrine changes post-COVID-19 with rising levels in females indicating persistent immunoendocrine shifts.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Modest but marked increase over time in females (from 2.18 µU/mL to 3.26 µU/mL, p=0.043); males remained stable.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Indicates persistent endocrine shifts in females; supports prolonged immunoendocrine surveillance in women post-COVID-19.

overall_summary: Thyroid hormone marker; consistently higher in males throughout post-COVID-19 follow-up, reflecting sex-based physiological differences.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Consistently higher in males compared to females throughout follow-up (e.g., Males 3.18 ng/L vs Females 2.95 ng/L at T0, p=0.0006).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Reflects innate sex-based physiological variations; lower levels in females may indicate vulnerability to endocrine shifts.

overall_summary: Thyroid hormone marker; shows slight increase over time post-COVID-19, particularly in males.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Slight increase over time in total population (p=0.010), with males showing increase from 1.15 ng/dL to 1.21 ng/dL (p=0.021).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Part of endocrine adaptation pattern post-COVID-19; relevant for long-term thyroid function monitoring.

overall_summary: Renal function marker; increases over time in both sexes post-COVID-19, with males consistently showing higher values indicating subtle renal adaptation.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Increased significantly over time in both sexes (females p=0.009, males p=0.001), consistently higher in males throughout follow-up.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Indicates sex-based differences in renal adaptation; males face higher physiological burden requiring monitoring.

overall_summary: Renal function and protein metabolism marker; consistently higher in males post-COVID-19, also increases with protein supplementation in active older adults.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated male survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Consistently higher in males throughout follow-up.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Reflects sex-based differences in renal function and potential higher acute physiological burden in males.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 12 weeks of daily milk protein supplementation in physically active older adults
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Increased significantly in the protein group (P Interaction < 0.001), no changes in placebo group.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Indicates altered protein metabolism with supplementation; not associated with adverse renal effects in this context.

overall_summary: Cardiac biomarker; decreases over time post-COVID-19 but males consistently show higher values indicating greater subclinical cardiac stress.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Decreased significantly in both sexes (females p=0.001, males p=0.003). Males consistently exhibited higher values, particularly during early follow-up.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Males face adverse risk for greater subclinical cardiac stress; supports early cardiac screening in men post-COVID-19.

overall_summary: Inflammatory marker (C-reactive protein); declines post-COVID-19 but males consistently show higher levels, indicating interconnected systemic inflammation.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significant decline over time in both sexes. Males consistently exhibited higher levels than females, particularly at T2 (p=0.016) and T3 (p=0.001).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Part of inflammation-cardiac stress correlation in males; supports sex-tailored inflammatory monitoring.

overall_summary: Coagulation and inflammatory marker; declines overall post-COVID-19 but remains consistently higher in females, indicating sustained elevation and delayed coagulative resolution.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Declined overall (p<0.001) but remained consistently higher in females compared to males across all timepoints (p<0.05).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Females show sustained fibrinogen elevation suggesting delayed coagulative resolution; supports prolonged inflammatory surveillance in women.

overall_summary: Immune cell marker; shows temporary surge in females post-COVID-19, reflecting transient adaptive immunity differences.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated female survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Modest but significant temporary increase in females at T2 (p=0.006).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Reflects transient adaptive immunity differences in females; part of sex-specific immune response pattern.

overall_summary: Coagulation marker; remains stable overall post-COVID-19 but significantly higher in females at 30-month endpoint, indicating potential for prolonged coagulation abnormalities.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-SARS-CoV-2 infection in vaccinated survivors
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Remained stable overall, but significantly higher in females compared to males at the 30-month (T3) endpoint (p=0.024).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Elevated D-dimer in females at 30-month suggests adverse risk for prolonged coagulation issues; supports extended surveillance in women.

overall_summary: White blood cell count; stable over time post-COVID-19 with males showing consistently higher values.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-COVID-19 hematological parameters
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Did not change significantly over time in overall cohort (p=0.422), but males consistently had higher values, particularly at T1 (p=0.001).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Reflects sex-based hematological differences; not a sensitive marker for post-COVID changes.

overall_summary: Lipid metabolism marker; shows sex-specific fluctuations post-COVID-19 with males having higher initial levels that decline while females show sustained increase.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: post-COVID-19 lipid metabolism
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Fluctuated slightly; males initially demonstrated higher levels which gradually declined, while females showed a sustained increase by T3.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Sex-specific lipid metabolism patterns post-COVID-19; linked to glucose metabolism changes.

overall_summary: Energy metabolism regulator derived from FNDC5; downregulated in HCC tissues and decreased in serum of HCC patients. Low preoperative levels predict postoperative complications after hepatectomy.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: HCC tissues (TCGA dataset) compared with noncancer tissues
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: FNDC5/irisin expression downregulated (P < 0.001).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Diagnostic utility for HCC; lower expression may reflect cancer-related energy metabolism alterations.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: HCC patients compared with healthy controls
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Serum irisin decreased: HCC 2.05 ± 0.83 µg/ml vs Healthy 3.16 ± 0.86 µg/ml (P < 0.001).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Novel diagnostic biomarker for HCC with AUC 0.8364, 76.9% sensitivity, 76.5% specificity at 2.62 µg/ml cutoff.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Prediction of postoperative complications after hepatectomy in HCC patients
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Low preoperative levels (≤2.62 µg/ml) significantly correlated with high CCI scores (P < 0.05).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Predictive biomarker for adverse surgical outcomes; low levels indicate higher complication risk and longer hospital stay.

overall_summary: Aggregated genetic risk score from multiple SNPs; significantly predicts epithelial ovarian cancer risk in general population and BRCA1/2 carriers across multiple ancestries.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: non-mucinous EOC risk in women of European ancestries
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Significant diagnostic utility for EOC risk stratification; enables personalized prevention strategies.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: non-mucinous EOC risk in women of East Asian ancestries
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: PRS demonstrates weaker but significant association in East Asian populations; ancestry-specific optimization needed.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: non-mucinous EOC risk in women of African ancestries
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Strong predictive utility in African ancestry populations comparable to European populations.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: EOC risk in BRCA1 pathogenic variant carriers
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Enhances risk prediction in high-risk BRCA1 carriers; supports integration into prevention programs.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: EOC risk in BRCA2 pathogenic variant carriers
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Higher predictive accuracy in BRCA2 vs BRCA1 carriers; substantial clinical utility for targeted screening.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Cumulative risk of EOC by age 80 in general population (99th vs 1st centile)
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: 99th centile: 2.24-2.81% vs 1st centile: 0.56-0.78% depending on model.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Demonstrates clear dose-response relationship for risk stratification; top percentiles warrant enhanced surveillance.

overall_summary: Mucosal immune function marker; maintained with probiotic supplementation in athletes, associated with reduced upper respiratory infections.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 14-week Lactobacillus probiotic intervention in elite athletes
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Maintained concentrations; reduced total number of upper respiratory infection days.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Protective benefit for immune health in athletes; probiotic supplementation supports mucosal immunity.

overall_summary: Pro-inflammatory cytokine mediating anti-viral and anti-bacterial immunity; restored by probiotic supplementation in fatigued athletes.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 4-week Lactobacillus probiotic intervention in fatigued athletes
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Restored to levels seen in healthy athletes.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Protective benefit; probiotic supplementation can restore immune function in fatigued athletic populations.

overall_summary: Intestinal barrier function marker; shows small to moderate improvement with probiotic supplementation in athletes.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Probiotic supplementation (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Streptococcus) for 4 weeks in male non-elite runners
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Small to moderate improvement.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Protective benefit for gut health; may help mitigate exercise-induced gastrointestinal discomfort.

overall_summary: Exercise performance metric; shows dose-dependent improvement with probiotic supplementation in non-elite athletes but no change in elite athletes.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Lactobacillus probiotic (30-90 billion CFU) for 6 weeks in non-elite athletes during treadmill testing
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Dose-dependent improvement.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Ergogenic benefit for non-elite athletes; probiotics may enhance endurance performance.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Probiotic formulation for 4 weeks in male non-elite runners
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Improved.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Supports probiotic use for performance enhancement in recreational athletes.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 14-week Lactobacillus intervention in elite athletes
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: No improvement.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Ceiling effect in elite athletes; probiotics may be more beneficial for non-elite populations.

overall_summary: Body composition marker; increases with protein supplementation combined with exercise in physically active older adults with low habitual protein intake.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 12 weeks of daily milk protein supplementation and walking exercise in physically active older adults
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Larger relative increase in protein group (Δ0.93 ± 1.22%) vs placebo (Δ0.44 ± 1.40%, P Interaction = 0.046). Truncal lean body mass also increased more (P Interaction = 0.007).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Protective benefit against sarcopenia; protein supplementation with exercise effectively improves body composition in older adults.

overall_summary: Body composition marker; decreases more with protein supplementation combined with exercise in physically active older adults.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 12 weeks of daily milk protein supplementation in physically active older adults
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Larger absolute decrease in protein group (Δ-0.90 ± 1.22 kg) vs placebo (Δ-0.31 ± 1.28 kg, P Interaction = 0.013); larger relative decrease (Δ-0.92 ± 1.19% vs Δ-0.39 ± 1.36%, P Interaction = 0.029).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Health improvement; reduced fat mass associated with lower cardiovascular and metabolic disease risks.

biomarker_name: Physical performance (Gait speed, Chair-rise, TUG, VO2max)
overall_summary: Functional performance metrics; improve with exercise training in older adults but protein supplementation does not provide additional benefit beyond exercise alone.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Walking exercise training with or without protein supplementation in physically active older adults
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: All measures improved significantly in both groups (P Time < 0.001), no significant between-group differences with protein supplementation.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Exercise is primary driver of functional improvement; protein supplementation benefits body composition but not additional performance gains in already active older adults.

overall_summary: Vitamin D status marker; increases over time in physically active older adults regardless of protein supplementation.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 12 weeks of intervention in physically active older adults
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Increased significantly in both groups (P Time = 0.001), no between-group differences.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Reflects seasonal/activity-related changes; not specifically influenced by protein supplementation.

overall_summary: Cell-derived vesicles shuttling biomolecules including miRNAs; significantly elevated in breast cancer patients and correlate with tumor burden, serving as potential cancer biomarkers.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Breast cancer patients vs healthy controls
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significantly more EVs in patient sera; Total EVs: BrCa 1.85 × 10^10/mL vs control 1.18 × 10^10/mL (p = 0.001).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Diagnostic utility for breast cancer; elevated EV counts associated with malignancy.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Tumour burden in murine breast cancer model
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Moderate positive correlation between serum EV number and tumour burden (rho = 0.386, p = 0.047).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Potential prognostic marker; EV quantity reflects disease burden.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Her2+ and TNBC breast cancer subtypes
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significant increase in both cancer groups vs controls; higher (non-significant) in Her2+ vs TNBC.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Subtype differences may exist; requires further investigation for specificity.

overall_summary: EV-encapsulated microRNA; significantly elevated in breast cancer patient sera when expressed as copies per EV, suggesting potential as novel circulating biomarker.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Breast cancer patient sera vs healthy controls
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significantly greater miR-451a copies/EV: BrCa 15.8 vs healthy 5.5 (p = 0.029); per exosomal EV: BrCa 38.60 vs healthy 11.63 (p = 0.019).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Novel diagnostic biomarker potential for breast cancer; approach accounting for EV number improves specificity.

overall_summary: EV-encapsulated microRNA; elevated in serum of breast cancer patients who develop distant metastases, serving as prognostic marker.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Metastatic progression in breast cancer patients
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significantly elevated in patients (n=16) who developed distant metastases compared to those (n=22) who did not.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Prognostic utility for metastatic breast cancer; may identify patients at higher risk for progression.

overall_summary: EV-encapsulated microRNA; elevated in plasma of breast cancer patients compared to healthy controls.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Plasma of breast cancer patients vs healthy controls
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significantly elevated in breast cancer patients (n=16) compared to healthy controls (n=16).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Diagnostic utility for breast cancer; part of multi-marker EV-miRNA panel potential.

overall_summary: Plasma EV-associated microRNA; elevated in breast cancer patients with high reported specificity for discrimination.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Plasma of breast cancer patients vs healthy controls
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Significantly elevated in breast cancer patients (n=16) compared to healthy controls (n=16).
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Diagnostic utility; previously reported 100% sensitivity and 92.9% specificity with specialized detection probe.

overall_summary: Serum EV-derived microRNA; elevated in breast cancer patients compared to healthy controls.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Serum-derived EVs of breast cancer patients
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Elevated in n=50 breast cancer patients vs n=12 healthy controls.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Potential diagnostic biomarker for breast cancer.

overall_summary: Serum EV-derived microRNA; elevated in breast cancer patients compared to healthy controls.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: Serum-derived EVs of breast cancer patients
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Elevated in n=50 breast cancer patients vs n=12 healthy controls.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Potential diagnostic biomarker for breast cancer.

overall_summary: Renal function marker; decreases over time with exercise training but not differentially affected by protein supplementation in healthy older adults.

findings_by_activity.activity_context: 12 weeks of protein supplementation in physically active older adults
findings_by_activity.effect_and_magnitude: Decreased in both groups over time (P Time < 0.001), no significant between-group differences.
findings_by_activity.clinical_implication: Protein supplementation does not adversely affect renal function in healthy older adults with normal baseline function.
